newsitem.title: UK: London Exchange tightens rules on AIM market.
newsitem.headline: London Exchange tightens rules on AIM market.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange said on Monday it tightened rules governing admission to the Alternative Investment Market, which was set up in 1995 to allow smaller companies to gain a quicker and simpler market listing.
The Exchange said companies would be required to disclose the name of anyone who has received fees or shares worth 10,000 stg or more in the 12 months to joining AIM.
The new rules also stipulated that the market should be immediately notified if the financial performance of the company fell short of projections made in their admission documents.
They also said there were be a greater emphasis on the specific responsibility of nominated advisers to satisfy themselves that a company was appropriate for admission to AIM.
The LSE said the new rules had been sent to all market participants, who had until June 16 to return their comments.
The final version will be published at the end of June.
